t: Section 866(f)(1) of the Ike Skelton National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2011 (Public Law 111–383; 124 Stat. 4296; 10 U.S.C. 2302 note) is amended by striking “the date that is five years after the date of the enactment of this Act.” and inserting “December 31, 2019.”.

fable.w: This section only extends a sunset date in an existing statute by replacing one expiration date with another. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside parties, rulemaking authority, or right to sue. There is no tempting reading here, since no actor outside the federal government is involved in any federal decision.
fable.s: is amended by striking “the date that is five years after the date of the enactment of this Act.” and inserting “December 31, 2019.”

qwen_block.w: This section is a technical amendment that changes a specific date in a previous statute. It does not establish any process for consultation, public comment, advisory boards, or coordination with outside parties. It is purely an internal legislative adjustment to a deadline.
qwen_block.s: Section 866(f)(1) of the Ike Skelton National Defense Authorization Act for Fiscal Year 2011 (Public Law 111–383; 124 Stat. 4296; 10 U.S.C. 2302 note) is amended by striking “the date that is five years after the date of the enactment of this Act.” and inserting “December 31, 2019.”.

opus.w: This is a technical amendment that changes an expiration date in an earlier law. It creates no comment period, hearing, advisory body, consultation with outside entities, or right to sue. The program it extends may involve outside parties, but this text itself sets up no process for outsiders to take part in a federal decision.
opus.s: is amended by striking “the date that is five years after the date of the enactment of this Act.” and inserting “December 31, 2019.”.
opus.b: 1. **Tempting reading:** Section 866 of the FY2011 NDAA set up a defense acquisition program that involves outside parties such as contractors or small businesses, so pushing back its end date might look like it supports participation. That reading fails because this section only replaces a sunset date. It says nothing about any outside party consulting on, commenting on, or challenging a federal decision.
